1. `general_agent/lifecycle.rs`: new `launch_delivery_failure` applies the same
   `surfaces_as_failure(SendOrigin::Programmatic)` contract. Bytes on the PTY =
   uncertainty the ledger keeps, not a spawn failure. A pre-write refusal
   (`pty_unavailable`, `tab_busy_refused`, `tab_not_reachable_on_peer`) still fails
   the spawn. No timer, no poll, no retry, and no change to the delivery path or
   the pending-delivery ledger.

   - `Tab::launch_session_authenticated()` (new, codeterm-pty types): agent_type +

     `rearm_authenticated_agent_input`.
   - `boot_stage::honest_boot_stage`: `emit_boot_stage` (the sole writer of
     SpawnFailed) refuses SpawnFailed when the tab is already at ProviderReady or
     AgentReady AND the launch nonce is proven.
   - `boot_stage::reconcile_boot_stage_with_session_binding`, called from
     `finish_session_binding` on `claim.nonce_verified`: a binding arriving after a
     latched failure retires it at the instant the proof lands. Event-driven by the
     hook report, never polled.
   - `void_launch_session_proof` retires the echoed nonce where the failure is
     itself evidence the process died (`LaunchFailure::proves_process_gone`:
     PtySpawn / PtyEof / TabClosed / ReaderSetup / ReaderRuntime), at
     `record_reader_termination`, and on the dead-PTY restore-failure path.
     Deadline and delivery faults do NOT void it. This is what keeps real failures
     latching.

Every other SpawnFailed writer (commands/pty.rs restore paths, orchestration_pair,
startup/servers, orchestrator early failures) emits from a stage at or below
AgentLaunching, so the guard is inert there by construction. The agent-restart path
clears identity and resets to PtyStarting before its readiness wait, so
